sources.citation: Lastra, Yolanda. 1990. El náhuatl del sur de Puebla. Anales de Antropología 27(1): 383-390. México: UNAM-IIA.
sources.note: Nothing. All nine PDF pages read eyes-on. The article is a dialect-survey follow-up (13 towns, Jan-Mar 1989) comparing /i/ for /e/, final -n, epenthetic /g/, glide insertion, vowel length, -li absolutive, continuative -tok/-tika, lexical isoglosses; Santa María la Alta (site 15, Santa Cruz Tlacotepec) is described pp. 388-389 as an outlier with no final -l or -k and -tika continuative, founded c. 1875-1900 by pastores from Tepelcahuaca, Guerrero ('speak a pastor dialect', abstract p. 390). No word 'acento'; forms cited without accent marks.

sources.citation: Hvilshøj, Ulrik. 2004. El dialecto pastor: Las afiliaciones dialectológicas del Nahuatl de los pastores. In Dehouve, Cervantes Delgado & Hvilshøj (eds.), La vida volante: Pastoreo trashumante en la Sierra Madre del Sur, ayer y hoy, 103-129. Universidad Autónoma de Guerrero.

sources.note: The only published study devoted to the pastores' Nahuatl, which Lastra 1990 identifies as the variety of Santa María la Alta; a 27-page dialectological comparison is the most likely place for a phonological/prosodic statement.

sources.note: The dialect survey behind Glottolog's classification; its questionnaire transcriptions mark stress whenever it is not penultimate (snippet 'El acento se marca cuando no recae en la penúltima sílaba o en monosílabos'), and it holds the Xochiltepec/Huatlatlauca points and the Zoyatlán (Guerrero) pastores point that Lastra 1990 says matches Santa María la Alta; the phonology chapter (1. Fonología) may carry an explicit accent remark for these points.
